statements.text: We don't want to get in the way, or have too much of a regulatory burden. We need progress; that's ultimately what drives our success in manufacturing, in AI and in the technology space. [...] But we have to do it within reason, and not at the expense of people in our communities.
statements.venue: CNN Politics article on data centers and the AI boom

statements.text: Any corporations looking to build data centers in our communities need to pay their own way, ensure that they are not polluting our land, air, or water, be clear and upfront about how much water they will use, and commit to transparency and community buy-in. That includes paying for the new power plants and transmission lines they need, being billed as their own class of customer so those costs don't land on household electric bills, and respecting community decisions on siting and permitting. Companies cannot come in promising jobs and investment and then leave taxpayers and ratepayers holding the bill.
I don't want them to come in on the backs of taxpayers, [...] And, local municipalities should have a voice on whether they want them or not.
statements.venue: Beloit Daily News, remarks on hyperscale data centers at a campaign stop

statements.text: They use our water and power, take our land, we get the bill,
statements.venue: Campaign TV ad "PULL" (as reported by WisPolitics)
